question.problem: If $\,u(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,v(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}]\,$ are solutions to ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$, find $Aw(t)$ where $w(t)=[\begin{aligned}9{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].$

current_example.problem: If ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117453/assets/46bdbb199d1f748bde7e92ee4e0d0ca034404b194cd794f19c6c6c55c09f1b1a.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117453/assets/2e150ed341157943cd4251b9cf46bade6de6fd64e34afce1c301106f7cf9daf8.svg) are solutions to $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t),$ find $A\mathbf{w}(t)$ where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14117453/assets/42af708789e15923eeacefaf297049d3fcd881fd6317060f4e1f02eb2e664127.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
Since $\mathbf{u}(t)$ and $\mathbf{v}(t)$ are solutions to $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t),$ the superposition principle guarantees that 

$$
c\mathbf{u}(t) + d\mathbf{v}(t)
$$

 is also a solution to $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)$ for all $c,d\in\mathbb{R}.$

Notice that 

$$
\mathbf{w}(t)=4\mathbf{u}(t)+6\mathbf{v}(t).
$$

 

Therefore, $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t).$ So, in order to find $A\mathbf{w}(t)$ we just need to find $\mathbf{w}'(t)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Aw & ={w}^{′}(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(4{e}^{4t})^{′} \\ (6{e}^{5t})^{′}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}16{e}^{4t} \\ 30{e}^{5t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
